A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SELF-REDTEAM and support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original appendices are retained and renumbered in v2, which adds Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and capability evaluations, training dynamics, attack-diversity measurements, and an appendix case study of emergent refusal.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen and Llama experiments, StrongREJECT evaluations, and multi-turn attack results in Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: The shared attacker–defender policy, hidden CoT, reward components, Re++ updates, and optional SFT objective are unchanged. Appendix A applies the existing procedure to additional checkpoints; multi-turn training remains future work.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds StrongREJECT evaluation and X-Teaming multi-turn attacks. The latter introduces an interactive adversarial scenario beyond v1's single-turn evaluations. Existing training datasets and evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 add Qwen2.5-Instruct reference baselines at 3B, 7B, and 14B. The existing Llama reference and comparison approaches—Defender-only, Defender-only + SFT, and Self-play without CoT—remain; no new competing training algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: New experiments use Qwen2.5 at three sizes and non-abliterated Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as training starting points, extending the original abliterated 8B configuration. Table 7 introduces evaluation on 50 HarmBench test behaviors with 10 attack plans per behavior across three turns. Original experiment settings remain documented unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a substantive robustness test: whether defenses trained exclusively on single-turn interactions transfer to multi-turn attacks, evaluated across four model configurations. Tables 3–6 also extend the existing CoT, SFT, and static-defender ablations to additional backbones. Earlier diversity and emergent-refusal analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains eight-run means and 95% confidence intervals, Figure 4 retains bootstrapped eight-checkpoint distributions, and the appendix variation estimates are unchanged. The new tables report point scores without specifying additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 add substantial results while original Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. For example, Table 5 reports Qwen2.5-14B WJB harmful ASR of 0.742 for the baseline versus 0.247 for Self-play; Table 7 reports Llama multi-turn ASR of 76% versus 42%. These are comparisons within new experiments, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its assumptions, game formulation, and proof are unchanged. The complete proof moves from Appendix A to Appendix B; the method's mathematical objectives are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning online self-play, safety guarantees, attack diversity, hidden CoT, and capability preservation. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations concerning generalization across model families and scales, stronger capability preservation for Qwen than Llama, and transfer beyond single-turn attack patterns. It labels the evidence preliminary, but its claim that safety gains do not cost performance overreaches the tables: Llama's AlpacaEval score falls from 24.74 to 20.62 even with Self-play + SFT.

D1.justification: Table 7 supplies the new multi-turn evaluation's behavior source, sample count, attack-plan budget, and turn limit; Tables 3–6 explicitly identify GPT-4o as the AlpacaEval comparison reference. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training-time estimates, templates, and code-access information remain unchanged, without detailed implementation updates for the expanded experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to StrongREJECT and X-Teaming for the new evaluations. The original cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior online and offline self-play approaches are retained.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a separate results appendix with a summary and three subsections, updates cross-references, and adds a preliminary-results pointer in the limitations paragraph. Existing prose and section order are largely unchanged; other edits include a more specific Figure 5 model name and an acknowledgment name correction.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables combining safety, benign compliance, and instruction-following results, plus a distinct paired baseline/Self-play table for multi-turn attacks. Original figures and Tables 1–2 are retained. The original appendix Table 3 becomes Table 8, and Figure 5 receives a small caption revision.

improvement.justification: Appendix A substantially reduces v1's explicitly acknowledged empirical limitations: reliance on one abliterated 8B training backbone and single-turn evaluations. Comparisons across Qwen scales, a safety-aligned Llama starting point, and multi-turn attacks materially strengthen evidence for applicability. The gains are qualified by incomplete settings and uncertainty documentation for the new experiments, and capability-preservation language that exceeds some table results. These weaknesses limit the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
